summary.intent: Determine whether phase 71 (share-invite security and IPNS data-integrity API) needed a discussion pass, then run the GSD planning workflow to produce executable PLAN.md files for the phase.
summary.outcome: Found the phase-71 discussion already existed on a separate branch and was fully resolved; rebased that branch onto main and ran gsd-plan-phase through research, validation, and pattern-mapping stages. The planner then surfaced that locked decision D-01 (vaults-based ownership check) would break shipped subfolder/file sharing; traced the bug with the user through concrete scenarios, determined the fix (check ipns_records.user_id instead), and committed an amended CONTEXT.md/DISCUSSION-LOG.md. The planner has not yet been re-spawned with the amendment.

repo: CipherBox: only child items (subfolders/files) can be shared, never the vault root itself — vaults table holds exactly one row per user (the vault root, inserted at /vault/init); children never get a vaults row
shares.root_ipns_name / share_invites.rootIpnsName is always a child node's IPNS name copied verbatim from the client DTO, with no server-side ownership verification prior to this phase

ipns_records.user_id is documented as a non-authoritative 'creator marker' (authority is the record's Ed25519 signature, not row ownership), but it's the only server-side signal recording who registered a given child IPNS name

readDescriptorRef/writeDescriptorRef (shares) and encryptedKey (invites) hold the shared node's root key ECIES-wrapped to the recipient's pubkey (direct share) or an ephemeral pubkey (link invite, private key lives only in the URL fragment); writeDescriptorRef presence = write grant (invariant T-66-E1/D-07)

The real access-control boundary for sharing is cryptographic: minting a valid writeDescriptorRef requires the sharer to actually hold the parent folder's keys via resolveShareWriteDescriptor — an attacker without those keys can only wrap garbage

vaults.owner_id is uniquely indexed (one vault row per user) and ipns_records.ipnsName is globally unique first-claimer-wins, which together make the vault-root ownership signal trustworthy even though child ownership isn't
shares.module.ts omits Vault from TypeOrmModule.forFeature — would cause a runtime DI failure for D-01's @InjectRepository(Vault) if not fixed (caught by the pattern-mapper agent)
getInvitesForItem filters by sharerId, so a spoofed invite targeting another user's subfolder only pollutes the attacker's own invite listing, not the victim's

code.finding: rootIpnsName is always set to the selected item's IPNS name (params.item.ipnsName), i.e. a child node, never the vault root
Same child-node rootIpnsName pattern used for direct (non-invite) shares
onShare is a context-menu action on an item inside a folder listing, confirming sharing is always triggered on children, never the vault root
Child IPNS nodes get an ipns_records row with user_id set to the creator at first publish

workflow: gsd-plan-phase pipeline: Research → Validation Architecture (required by Nyquist Dimension 8) → drift/UI/security gates → pattern-mapping → planner spawn, with explicit commit checkpoints between stages
Known GSD quirk: a 'commit_failed' status during gate checks can be a false negative — verify via git log/show before retrying the commit
gsd-plan-phase does not auto-commit PATTERNS.md; it must be committed explicitly after the pattern-mapper returns
workflow.tdd_mode is persisted config and should be checked before treating planner-injected contributions (e.g. schema-gate, TDD hooks) as active
Nyquist validation Dimension 8 requires a '## Validation Architecture' section sourced from RESEARCH.md — this is the deciding factor for whether to run research before planning

friction: Locked decision D-01 from the prior phase-71 discussion assumed rootIpnsName always equals the vault root; this was falsified by actual code behavior and only surfaced during planning, forcing a mid-planning re-discussion
intel API-surface regen returned symbolCount 0 (regex extraction found nothing), producing an effectively empty hint that still had to be passed to the pattern-mapper flagged as incomplete
User interrupted an in-progress manual ROADMAP SC#3 edit to redirect toward letting GSD tooling own roadmap updates instead
open_items: ROADMAP.md SC#3 still references the dropped root-uniqueness partial index (from abandoned precondition #4); needs trimming, deferred to GSD tooling per user's instruction
D-01 amended (ipns_records.user_id check replaces vaults-based check) and committed to CONTEXT.md/DISCUSSION-LOG.md, but the planner has not yet been re-spawned with the amendment
Scenario D (attacker can create a cryptographically inert share/invite pointing at another user's subfolder they don't hold keys for) accepted as low-severity status quo, not tracked as a fix

Properly closing Scenario D would require persisting root_node_id (touches /vault/init, previously deferred in D-02) or a key-possession challenge (deferred to a future crypto phase) — neither is being pursued now
